      Create an account, download the app for your platform, sign in with the same email, and press connect. The app picks the fastest server near you on its own; the country list is there when you want to choose for yourself. No configuration files, no manual keys.

      WireGuard by default, because it is the fastest to connect and the lightest on battery, with OpenVPN over UDP and TCP available for networks that block it. Automatic is the right setting for almost everyone — the app falls back on its own when a network refuses the first choice.

      Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, Apple Pay and Google Pay. We never see or store your card number. The charge shows on your statement under our billing descriptor, and every payment produces a downloadable invoice in My Account.

      Our servers run from RAM and keep no persistent disk, so a machine that is powered down keeps nothing. There are no connection logs, no traffic logs and no DNS logs to hand over — a seized server holds the software that routes traffic and nothing that identifies who sent it.

      Independent audit — status

      No independent audit has been completed yet. We run RusVPN as a no-log service — no traffic logs, no DNS query logs, no connection timestamps tied to an account — and we have committed to having that claim examined by an outside firm rather than asking you to take our word for it.

      Until a report exists and is published here in full, we do not describe the service as “audited”. A claim you cannot check is not evidence, and a seal with nothing behind it is worth less than saying so plainly.

      Scope to be assessed
      Connection, traffic and DNS logging across all production regions
      Auditor
      Not yet appointed
      Report
      Will be published here in full, including any findings against us

      Last reviewed 11 August 2026.

      Usability research — status

      We test the experience the same way we treat the no-log claim: by checking, not asserting. So far this has been an expert usability review with a modeled five-participant benchmark — a structured walkthrough of the discovery, pricing, checkout and account flows.

      It is useful for finding and fixing problems; it is not a recruited real-user study, and we do not present its numbers as one. What it flagged, we changed rather than filed away: a confusing sign-in screen (a “confirm password” field on the login state) and competing calls-to-action are both fixed — login now asks only for email and password, and the funnel leads with one primary action.

      Method
      Expert usability review + modeled 5-participant benchmark — not recruited users
      Changed so far
      Sign-in simplified, calls-to-action unified — both already live on this page
      Next
      A recruited real-user study, published here in full including any findings against us

      Last reviewed 12 August 2026.

      Accessibility — status

      The site is built to WCAG 2.2 AA, and we would rather show the work than wear a badge. Every text colour clears its required ratio on the surface it sits on — 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large display type; the brand red is darkened on buttons so white still clears 4.5:1 at the lightest point of the gradient. Focus is always visible at a consistent 3px ring, motion honours prefers-reduced-motion, every field is labelled, and dialogs trap focus, close on Esc and return focus to where you left.

      Automated testing (axe-core, WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A & AA) reports zero violations. That is the floor, not the finish line: automated tools cannot judge a screen-reader journey, so we do not claim more than we have checked.

      Standard
      WCAG 2.2 level AA — contrast, focus, labels, motion, dialogs
      Verified (automated)
      Zero automated violations; keyboard path, visible focus, dialog focus-trapping and status-message announcements confirmed by an AT-API + keyboard audit
      Verified (screen reader)
      Recorded VoiceOver / Safari (iOS) listen-through, 12 Aug 2026 — recording on file
      Not yet
      A Windows High-Contrast (forced-colors) review — in progress

      Last reviewed 12 August 2026.
